title: Drift & Coherence Review (run 6, trend vs the 2026-11-06 run 5): the 7–9 Nov window, round 1 of Harbour carries the loop (LIN-4344), both repos; the first drift run to feed the area notes
description:
## As asked

<!-- harbour-periodical-gate id="drift-coherence-review" -->
Operator note: Read the window 7 Nov 00:00 UTC to 9 Nov 00:00 UTC (round 1 of "Harbour carries the loop", LIN-4344; main up to b315e0e8f) in both repos. This reading is the coherence baseline for the work that follows, so read only that window.

**Drift & Coherence Review, run 6 (trend vs the 2026-11-06 run 5).** This is the trend-aware periodical (`drift-coherence` in `lib/periodicals.js`, series anchor LIN-369). It looks for code that is locally right while the system as a whole drifts apart. **This task is the review itself.** You write the report, write its area-note entries, merge them in one docs-only PR, get the second read, comment and close. You mint no follow-up tickets.

Repositories: JKershaw/LinearViewer (Harbour) and JKershaw/simple-dispatcher (SD). Both are in scope.

## What was found when this task was minted (2026-11-10). Re-check all of it at HEAD.

**The window, pinned.**

* **Harbour:** `aec9e16be4afa9793a34cefe6a49a8eecd90736c..b315e0e8f3e1e5f3b5d6e634e53c5dc83b41d754`. That is 39 first-parent commits, from LIN-4340 (#2343) through LIN-4394 (#2382). Production (`lib routes public server.js`) is about 103 files, +5806 / −1597, the largest window this series has read. Recompute these figures.
* **SD:** `07c88f7a338b3e19a01070775e1f4d4cfc91f040..5d8489e7fd8434f0e69af7df11a3746790abbe64`. That is 7 commits (#329–#335) and about 20 files, +1875 / −116. SD had no commits between run 5 and 7 Nov, so here the window start and the previous edition's measured commit are the same.
* **The gap, outside the window.** Run 5 measured Harbour at `5c63aa261a2de891907c9b8d567f9932ed1985d0`. The 13 commits `5c63aa26..aec9e16be` came after it and before the window. They are LIN-4311, LIN-4312, LIN-4322, LIN-4254 anchors, run 5's own report, the paper and the essays. Their production diff is 4 files, +161 / −58. The contract measures the census against the previous report's commit (`5c63aa26`), but the operator says to read only the window. So run the census at `aec9e16be` as well, and label any movement that falls inside the gap as "outside the window", not as a finding. If main has moved past `b315e0e8f` by the time you run, report the later commits as an addendum and use none of them for a figure. This is run 5's own practice.

**What the window built** (from commit subjects; read the code, not this list):

* **As asked:** LIN-4351/4352/4353/4360/4362, `lib/as-asked-seal.js`, the brief composer and the proxy guard.
* **Size of the move:** LIN-4345/4367/4368/4369, and LIN-4393, which removed the setting inside the window. Check for residue.
* **The leftover step:** LIN-4373/4374/4375/4376. `LEFTOVER_RULE` in `lib/prompts/leftover-words.js` is meant to be its one home.
* **Area notes and look-first:** LIN-4371/4372/4383/4346/4370.
* **Periodicals feed notes:** LIN-4379/4380.
* **One issue access:** LIN-4354/4361.
* **LIN-4358:** model facts from the OpenRouter catalog, and the call budget.
* **LIN-4378:** the per-credential rate limit, the broker's 429 backoff, and the runner contract (LIN-4384/4385 in both repos). `lib/runner-kit/contract.json` grew by 374 lines and is pinned by sha256 in SD's `test/fixtures/runner-contract.json`.
* **Smaller pieces:** LIN-4381 (landed lane state), LIN-4382 (autopilot precedence), LIN-4349 (tail drives review in place).

Much of this window *creates* canonical homes: "one home", "one reader", "one adapter". A real finding is a decision that kept a second home after its first home landed.

**The previous edition.** `docs/reviews/drift-coherence-review-2026-11-06.md` (run 5, LIN-4324, PR #2334, merged as `b9fc60abc`). It measured Harbour at `5c63aa26` and SD at `07c88f7a`. Its compact trend ledger has 141 rows, with a machine copy at `docs/reviews/_evidence-2026-11-06-drift/ledger-run5.tsv`. Carry every row under its stable name and give each a run-6 delta. Retire a row only explicitly. Rows still open, with their homes as of minting (check each ticket's state):

* 137 `enqueue-route-list-restated` (LIN-4320)
* 141 `session-lane-grant-from-client-text` (LIN-4318)
* 131 `override-kind-list-stale` (LIN-4302)
* 135 `in-progress-predicate-server-client-split` (LIN-4256)
* 138 `element-method-guard-idiom-beyond-scan` (LIN-4303)
* 140 `working-beat-grammar-cross-repo` (LIN-3828)
* 136, 139 and 134, report-only
* 114, the halt cold-cache row, which is John's ruling

Run 5 was written before area notes existed, so this is the first drift run that writes to them.

## Audit the scope before you run it

Treat everything above as a starting point to widen, not a checklist to stay inside. Before you review, look for surfaces that are in remit but not listed here, and fold them in. A scope you could only shrink is suspect. Places to start:

* **Cross-repo duplication that is there by design but can still drift.** Two examples: the area-notes format and guard, copied into both repos (SD `docs/areas/README.md` says so, with `test/area-notes.test.js` against Harbour's `tests/unit/area-notes.test.js`), and the broker's 429 constants, held in both repos.
* **Prompt words that now have one home.** Check `LEFTOVER_RULE`, `GROUNDING_BY_KIND` and the As-asked block's words for re-statements elsewhere, including in SD and in `docs/`.
* **The seams between sibling reviews.** These sibling reports overlap the window or sit right next to it:
  * Seams & Tangles run 10: `docs/reviews/seams-tangles-review-2026-11-08-run10.md`. It names `seam:runner-contract` across both repos, `knot:agent-api<->other-features` through `lib/as-asked-seal.js`, and new hubs.
  * Design & Interface run 10: `docs/reviews/design-interface-review-2026-11-08.md`.
  * Stability run 5: `docs/reviews/stability-review-2026-11-08.md`.
  * Comprehension-Debt: `docs/reviews/comprehension-debt-review-2026-11-05.md`.
  * Code Quality: `docs/reviews/code-quality-review-2026-11-04.md`.

  Don't re-flag what they own: per-module quality belongs to Code Quality, and coupling structure to Seams. A surface no single review owns is in this one's scope.
* **Known-issues surfaces.** Read both repos' `CLAUDE.md`, the existing area notes, inline `TODO`/`FIXME` markers added in the window, and open tickets.

Be broad in what you search and bounded in what you report. The wider scope changes only what you examine, not what you report.

## Run the review

Work at the cross-cutting altitude, where code is locally right but globally drifting. Use the repos' own conventions as the reference and introduce no new tooling. Assess:

* **Duplication:** a decision re-implemented where one shared implementation is canonical. Coincidental similarity is fine.
* **Convention fragmentation:** competing patterns where one is canonical. Flag the outliers.
* **Dependency direction:** imports that run against the repo's own layering. Run 5 measured 0 `lib/` → `routes/` imports, two SCCs and its import walker (`_evidence-2026-11-06-drift/import-walker.mjs`). Re-measure.

These classes are a floor, not a ceiling: find the full set for this remit from the repo. For each finding, name the concrete cost a change would hit, not a style preference. No cosmetic churn.

**The census.** Use `scripts/code-shape/census-review.mjs <repo> <commit> [previousCommit]`; read its section in `scripts/code-shape/README.md` first. Run 5's scope flag was `--include '^(server\.js$|(lib|routes|public)/.*\.[cm]?js$)'`.

* **The area guide moved in the window.** `scripts/code-shape/areas.json` (git blob `642e9405`, the guide runs 4 and 5 used) was removed. The product registry `docs/areas/areas.json` replaced it (LIN-4371), and the tool's default now resolves through `lib/prompts/area-registry-path.js` (LIN-4383). The registry was also edited in the window (#2367 added `catalog-rate`).
* **Use one guide for every run, passed explicitly with** `--areas`**.** Use the HEAD registry, and record its sha256 and blob.
* **Then do a guide-only check at the baseline:** old guide against new guide, so that a map edit is not read as code moving. Seams run 10 did the same check (its §0).
* **First, reproduce run 5's census at** `5c63aa26` **with run 5's guide.** The tool changed in the window (the `claimedBy` move, the default path). If the reproduction is not byte-equal to `_evidence-2026-11-06-drift/census-run5-HEAD-5c63aa26-vs-af55cb73.json`, say why before you use the tool.
* **Record full commits for every run:** HEAD against `5c63aa26`, and `aec9e16be` for the gap.
* **SD:** if run 5 ran the census on SD, do the same here. If it did not, the SD census at `5d8489e` is a baseline and you say so.
* **Report the results as two compact tables.** In the first, give every `mustRule` group one ruling: real (the one place the decision should live and why, or both claimants and your pick), borderline, or noise, each with a one-line reason. A ruling is your finding, not a question to anyone. In the second, list the `table` groups with no ruling. Write prose and note entries only for real groups and for changes since run 5.
* **If the tool cannot run,** say so and review by hand as before.

## The report

* **Where it goes.** `docs/reviews/drift-coherence-review-<run date>.md` in LinearViewer, which is where all runs of this series live, with an evidence folder `docs/reviews/_evidence-<run date>-drift/`. If a sibling review already took that date, add a run suffix as run 4 did.
* **Its shape.** The report is severity-ranked and uncapped. Nothing, one thing or many are all valid results. Ground every finding in the source at HEAD, not in earlier prose. Give each finding a delta against run 5: new, unchanged, improved, worsened or resolved.
* **Per-area verdicts.** Give a verdict for each area the window touched: better, worse or neutral. This reading is the coherence baseline for the LIN-4344 work that follows.
* **The trend ledger.** Close with a compact ledger: every row under its stable name, with its severity and its run-6 delta.

## Feed the area notes, and mint no follow-up tickets

* **Where the notes are.** Harbour: `docs/areas/` (`README.md`, `areas.json`, guard `tests/unit/area-notes.test.js`, a 6144-byte cap per note). SD: `docs/areas/` (its own `README.md`, `areas.json` and guard `test/area-notes.test.js`). Follow each README's own rules, not this summary.
* **Notes at the cap.** At minting, Harbour's `runs-and-dispatch.md` was 6142 bytes and `llm-and-prompts.md` was 6073 bytes. Any entry there needs pruning and distilling first.
* **Where to look first.** List the files changed in `5c63aa26..HEAD` in each repo (in SD, `07c88f7a..HEAD`) and map each one to its area through the registry, so the reading starts where the work landed. Keep gap files apart from window files.
* **Which entry to write.**
  * A finding that leaves work in an area gets a Waiting entry.
  * A rule a builder there must follow gets a Lesson.
  * Each entry cites the area's file first, names its source as "(Drift & Coherence Review, <run date>)", and cites the report second.
  * A finding already filed as a ticket stays in the report only. That includes every carried row with a ticket.
  * In each note you touch, prune entries that are settled or no longer true.
* **SD entries.** A Harbour path is not a path in SD, so SD entries name the report in prose ("Harbour's docs/reviews/…"), as SD's README requires.
* **Routing findings with no area note.** A larger tidy becomes a Waiting entry worded as the size of the move, and is also listed for the person in the closing comment. A finding with no area file to cite (manifests, lockfiles, a live secret) goes in the closing comment, addressed to the person, never in a ticket. A cross-area seam goes under the area a change would start from, naming the other side, and the report says plainly that seams have no full home in the notes yet.
* **The PR.** Commit the report, the evidence and the Harbour note edits in **one docs-only PR** on LinearViewer. Rebase it onto main, and get it green under the notes guard and `ci-success`. If an SD note needs an entry, that edit can only land in SD, so open one companion docs-only PR there, cross-link the two, and merge both. On SD, CI is citeable, not enforceable, so read the check yourself before you merge. Prefer keeping a cross-repo seam under the Harbour area it starts from, where that is honest.

## Stay review-only

Change no code, config, guide or secret, and no doc beyond the report, its evidence folder and the area-note edits. An instruction not to touch files means the code and docs under review. It never covers this task's own deliverables.

## Adversarial second read (required before Done)

After the report and the note edits are written, a genuinely separate reader answers one question cold: *"What is the largest item in this window that this report missed or misfiled?"*

* **Which reader counts.** Tier 1, a wholly separate session, is preferred. Tier 2, a fresh-context sub-agent with no memory of the report-writing turn, is accepted. Tier 3, this same session re-reading its own report, is **not** accepted. State the tier you used.
* **The gate comment.** Post one comment on this task that contains all three of these lines in a single body:
  * `Adversarial second-read verdict: AGREE` or `Adversarial second-read verdict: DISAGREE`
  * `Differed from top finding: YES` or `Differed from top finding: NO`, meaning whether the reader's answer differed from the report's top finding, whatever the verdict
  * `Disposition: fixed in place`, `Disposition: escalated` or `Disposition: no change`

  The engine refuses Done until all three are present together.
* **The report's copy.** Copy the same three fields into a `## Adversarial Second-Read` section of the report, with the tier, the question and the reader's full answer.
* **What the verdict means.** AGREE and DISAGREE both conclude normally. A DISAGREE is itself the escalation.

## Conclude

1. Merge your own docs-only PR(s) once the required checks are green.
2. Post a concise, severity-ranked summary comment on this task. It links the report and names the merged PR(s). It also lists for the person any larger tidy, and any finding with no area file to cite.
3. Move this task to Done.

A review task left open is recommended again forever. You may conclude with a PR still open only if merging is genuinely impossible. Then name the blocker in the closing comment as an explicit handoff.

*End of what was asked. Steps write below this line; nothing above it changes.*

## Size of the move

**Size:** just the task
**Why:** Delivers the run-6 review, its area-note entries, merged docs-only PRs, second read and closure as asked; no Survey finding binds, since copied scripts, note eviction and ledger retirement are nearby work the review succeeds without.
**Cuts:** none
**Decided by:** the standing policy

## Implementation Plan

**What this is for.** Run 6 of the Drift & Coherence series reads the 7–9 Nov window (Harbour `aec9e16be..b315e0e8f`, SD `07c88f7a..5d8489e`) for decisions that kept a second home after their canonical home landed, and is the coherence baseline for the LIN-4344 work that follows. It is also the first drift run to write area notes. Nothing in the ticket has drifted from its purpose.

**Done looks like (the ticket's own Done-when, restated).** One docs-only Harbour PR (report, evidence folder, Harbour note edits) merged green under the notes guard and `ci-success`; the second-read gate comment and the report's `## Adversarial Second-Read` section carry the same three fields; a severity-ranked closing comment links the report and PR and lists any larger tidy and any finding with no area file; LIN-4403 is Done. No code, config or guide changes and no tickets minted.

**Cuts to** `## As asked`**: none.** Every clause is delivered in full. Two choices that look like cuts are not: no SD companion PR (decision 4 below, which the ask allows: "if an SD note needs an entry"), and SD gets a baseline census rather than a trend (run 5 never ran SD, so there is nothing to trend against).

**Facts this plan stands on** (read at HEAD this pass; the research comment holds the measurements, I re-checked the ones the work hinges on). Harbour `origin/main` is still `b315e0e8f`, SD `5d8489e`, so no addendum; nothing the ticket names changed since it was created. `runs-and-dispatch.md` is 6142 and `llm-and-prompts.md` 6073 of 6144 bytes; `agent-api.md` is 2358. `RESUMABLE_TARGETS`, `NEVER_RAN` and the inline `'pause'`/`'stop'` test sit in `lib/dispatch-leftover.js` beside `HALT_MODES` in `lib/workspace-halt.js` and a second archive-status pair in `lib/dispatch-store.js` (`_releaseIfHeld`). `isHermeticTestToken` has users in `lib/dispatch-entrance.js` and `lib/dispatch-factory.js`, so the `lib/should-mock-ai.js` note claim "nothing uses it" is false. `lib/periodicals.js` `areaNotes` restates routing rules. The run-5 reading it trends against is `docs/reviews/drift-coherence-review-2026-11-06.md` with evidence in `_evidence-2026-11-06-drift/`. The window's note-routing prompt words (`lib/periodicals.js`, `lib/prompts/leftover-words.js`) are code under review here, not rules for this review: where they disagree with the ask, the ask wins.

**Findings the report carries** (severity order; each is confirmed again at HEAD by the builder before it is written, and a finding that does not survive is dropped or re-ranked, not kept for symmetry):

1. **R1** `leftover-gate-restates-three-decisions`, LOW–MEDIUM, new: `lib/dispatch-leftover.js` restates session targets (home `lib/dispatch-targets.js`), the halt modes (home `HALT_MODES`; a third mode would read as "not halted" and queue a leftover during a halt) and the never-ran archive statuses (a second copy in the store; no exported home). Proposed homes: import `HALT_MODES` and the target decision; export the status set from the store. Census ranks 21 and 47 are these. Routed to `runs-and-dispatch.md` as a Waiting entry; the `lib/pipeline-churn.js` literal `'leftover'` folds into the existing `ORCHESTRATION_KINDS` entry for that file.
2. **P1–P4**, LOW, new, routed to `llm-and-prompts.md`: P1 `periodical-notes-bullet-restates-leftover-rule`; P2 `context-not-scope-three-homes` (Harbour formatter + both READMEs); P3 `area-notes-dir-outside-registry-path` (four spellings of `docs/areas/`); P4 `area-notes-guard-copied-and-diverged` (SD guard adds `sh` and three checks; SD README lacks the Periodical-entry rules; only comments hold the copies together). Fold P1–P3 into one entry if the byte budget needs it; P4 is a cross-repo seam and is worded as one.
3. **A1/A2 borderline**, LOW (the "no step may change them" sentence in two places; prompt literals beside four exported constants): one `agent-api.md` Waiting entry. Rate-limit "per token" wording is already noted; the report adds that it is inexact for unproven credentials (per IP) and the unpinned draft-6 `RateLimit-*` names, both report-only.
4. **Cross-repo conclusions, report-only**: runner contract is a full byte copy (`602ab014…eb40` both sides), rows 38/34 → 66/66 so run 5's mismatch is resolved; broker 429 policy and `DONE:`/`[done]` reading are designed duplicates held by contract rows; the check is one-way; the model-family mirror is unchanged (LIN-4301); size-policy residue is historical rows, not drift.

**Decisions and why.**

1. *Evidence is regenerated, not recovered.* Research outputs lived in a scratchpad. The builder re-runs `census-review.mjs` (scope `^(server\.js$|(lib|routes|public)/.*\.[cm]?js$)`, `--areas` explicit every time) and run 5's `import-walker.mjs` **in place**, commits outputs only, and adds no script copy. Reason: a fifth copy is the duplication this review exists to find. Witness: output sha256 prefixes match the research (census end-vs-run5 `88597e12`, end-vs-window-start `b0635c31`, guide-only `004bc1b3`, reproduction `1172e9e3`; graphs `67506a83` run 5, `4df7c047` window start, `49ff7f4d` end). A mismatch is explained in the report before the figure is used; it is not quietly accepted. Record the two guide identities (old blob `642e9405`; HEAD registry blob `4011e82a`, sha256 `74829793…f1d`) and full commits for every run.
2. *Gap versus window.* Run the census at `aec9e16be` too; the one disappearance against run 5 (`paint`/`paintCloseOut`) is labelled "outside the window", not a finding.
3. *Census rulings.* Two tables as asked: every `mustRule` group gets one ruling (ranks 21, 47 real → R1; 3, 6, 39, 43, 93, 114 noise; 167 borderline, already noted; 8, 18, 102–104, 379 carry run 5's ruling; the 92 unchanged rows join to run 5 by content, not rank), and the tabled groups listed without ruling. SD's census is labelled a first baseline (61 / 27 / 25).
4. *No SD companion PR.* P4 is a cross-repo seam whose fix starts from Harbour's copy, and the ask prefers keeping a seam under the Harbour area it starts from "where that is honest". It is honest here: the SD-side gap is the README and guard drift, which the Harbour entry names in prose. The report says plainly that seams have no full home in the notes yet. If the builder finds a genuinely SD-local item while writing, that alone opens the SD PR (docs-only, cross-linked, CI read by hand before merging).
5. *Notes at the cap.* Order: prune what is false at HEAD (the `should-mock-ai.js` claim), fold same-file entries, distil without changing meaning, then add. Never remove a true unticketed entry to make room; required routing wins over the Survey's report-only fallback. Each prune or distil is recorded in the report. Entries cite the area's file first, name "(Drift & Coherence Review, 10 Nov)" and cite the report second; cite files, never lines. A finding already filed as a ticket (the six carried rows) stays in the report only.
6. *Ledger.* Carry every run-5 row under its stable name with a run-6 delta, a severity and a new "noted in `<slug>.md`" column (this stops a finding having a ledger row and an unlinked note entry). Row count is set from the run-5 TSV (141), not the research's 51+3+90=144, which double-counts rows citing both window and gap files. The builder runs the touch map in place and states the real counts. New rows are added for R1, P1–P4 and the borderlines. Retire a row only explicitly. Rows 137, 141, 131, 135, 138, 140 are checked against their tickets' state (all Backlog at research time); 114 keeps John's ruling; 136, 139, 134 stay report-only.
7. *Per-area verdicts*, written from the evidence, provisional: LLM & prompts better (one home each for as-asked, size, model facts; residue P1–P4), Runs & dispatch neutral (R1 adds second homes), Agent API neutral, the rest neutral.

**Order of landing.** (1) Branch from current `origin/main`; commit evidence. (2) Report. (3) Note edits (prune first). (4) Tier-2 second read: a fresh-context sub-agent given the window, both repos and the finished report, asked cold only "What is the largest item in this window that this report missed or misfiled?"; it must not be given this plan's conclusions. Fix in place if it finds something real, otherwise record "no change"; copy its full answer, tier, question and the three gate fields into the report's `## Adversarial Second-Read` section before the PR is final. (5) Rebase, green under `tests/unit/area-notes.test.js` and `ci-success`, merge. (6) Post the gate comment (all three lines in one body), then the closing comment, then Done. If main moves, later commits go in an addendum and feed no figure. If the run date is taken by a sibling report, add a run suffix as run 4 did.

**How we know every place is found.** The second-home sweep covered the 12 new modules, the 25 most-changed files and every new constant; the census covers clones and constants mechanically; the touch map covers ledger rows; the second read is the independent catch for what these miss. This plan names what they cannot catch (decisions expressed in prose, prompts and docs rather than code), and the second read's job is exactly those.

**Likeliest ways this breaks.**

1. *Notes guard goes red at the end* (byte cap, first path not in the area, report path missing). Witness: run `tests/unit/area-notes.test.js` and `wc -c` on each touched note after every note edit, not only at the end.
2. *A figure no longer reproduces* because the wrong guide, an unpinned commit, or a copied script was used. Witness: the hash prefixes above, fail before the evidence is regenerated and pass after.
3. *A finding is judged by the window's own words* ("one home" claims in commit messages, the routing bullet in `lib/periodicals.js`). Witness: every finding cites source at HEAD, and the second read reads the source cold.
4. *Scope creep into fixes* (editing the code that R1 points at, copying scripts). Witness: `git diff --stat origin/main...HEAD` lists only `docs/reviews/` and `docs/areas/` paths.

**Witnesses for what is promised.** Report present with every finding delta-labelled against run 5; the run-5 row names are a subset of the run-6 ledger (diff of the name columns is empty); two census tables present and every `mustRule` group has a ruling; area-note guard and `ci-success` green; the gate comment contains `Adversarial second-read verdict:`, `Differed from top finding:` and `Disposition:` and matches the report section; no ticket created (the issue's relations and children stay empty). No validation, contract or guard is loosened.

**Session fit:** fits one session

plan-review due: no

*Reason for no review:* docs-only, one repo, no credentials, merge rules or dispatch contract touched; the one risky step (the second read) is itself a required independent reader.

**Changelog.** Replaced the research notes with this plan (the research comment keeps the measurements). Resolved the three open questions: ledger rows are the run-5 TSV's 141, not 144; no SD companion PR; A1/A2 become one `agent-api.md` entry.

comments.body:
## Survey open-0: LIN-4403 @ b315e0e8f

origin/main is `b315e0e8f`, the pinned window end, so there's no addendum. SD main is `5d8489e7f`. I re-checked the window figures and they match: 39 first-parent commits; production 103 files, +5806/−1597; gap 4 files, +161/−58.

**Why this will be hard**

1. **The review is reading the code that writes its own instructions.** The window built the surfaces this task works through: the area registry, the census default path (LIN-4383), and the "periodicals feed notes" routing words (`lib/periodicals.js:316`). Those routing words are restated nearly word for word in this ticket. The reviewer will be tempted to judge them by their own standard. Treat them as code under review, not as the review's rules.
2. **The volume is large, and the hard part is the final steps.** The work covers 141 carried ledger rows, two repos, two notes at the cap (`runs-and-dispatch.md` is 6142/6144 bytes, `llm-and-prompts.md` is 6073), and a separate second reader. It also means merging in two repos and closing to Done. Pruning those notes means ruling on entries the window itself wrote: LIN-4369 added "two notes, two lessons" and LIN-4378 added Waiting entries. If pruning slips, the guard turns red at the end.
3. **"One home" is often already claimed in comments.** Many window commits are self-audits ("leftovers", "close-out tidy: … one owner"). A finding has to beat the author's own claim, using the source.

**Already de-risked (I ran these, read-only, with the HEAD tool and run 5's scope flag)**

- **Reproduction.** I ran `census-review.mjs` at `5c63aa26` vs `af55cb73` with run 5's guide (`areas-run5.json` has sha256 `e3194f52…`, identical to blob `642e9405`).
